question: At 1150 kg, what is the recommended airspeed for an engine failure after take-off with flaps in T/O?
explanation: At 1150 kg the airspeed for an engine failure after take-off (flaps T/O) is 72 KIAS - at 1000 kg it is 66 KIAS, and at 850 kg it is 59 KIAS.

question: At 1150 kg, what is the best glide angle airspeed with flaps UP?
explanation: Best glide angle airspeed at 1150 kg, flaps UP, is 73 KIAS - this figure recurs throughout Chapter 3 for gliding, restarts and emergency landings at max mass.

question: During engine problems on the ground, what must be done immediately if the oil pressure is in the red range?

options.text: The problem must be monitored for one minute before acting
The ECU must be swapped to ECU B
The engine must be shut down immediately
Power lever must be reduced to IDLE only

explanation: If the oil pressure is in the red range during ground engine problems, the engine must be shut down immediately.

question: If an engine problem occurs during take-off and the take-off can no longer be aborted with a safe height not yet reached, what should the pilot do?

options.text: Turn back immediately to the departure airfield
Climb to circuit altitude before deciding on a landing area
Select ECU B and continue the take-off regardless
Carry out a straight-ahead emergency landing; do not attempt to turn back to the airfield

explanation: The AFM warns explicitly against turning back - a straight-ahead emergency landing must be carried out, because turning back can be fatal.

question: During engine problems in flight with the engine running roughly, which switch selection is part of the checklist if time allows?
explanation: After checking the engine caution light and fuel system items, the checklist calls for ECU SWAP to ECU B; if this does not solve the problem, switch back to AUTOMATIC.

question: During a loss of engine power in flight, what is the purpose of switching the ENGINE MASTER OFF then ON again?

options.text: It resets the propeller governor to fine pitch
It transfers fuel from the AUX to the MAIN tank
It tests the ECU Backup Battery

explanation: After trying ECU B, the checklist for loss of power includes an 'ECU reset' by cycling ENGINE MASTER OFF then ON.

question: What is the maximum airspeed for windmilling the propeller?
explanation: The maximum airspeed for windmilling is 110 KIAS; higher airspeeds may result in propeller overspeed.

question: Restarting the engine with a windmilling propeller is possible within which airspeed range?
explanation: A windmilling restart is possible at airspeeds between 73 and 110 KIAS, and at altitudes below the engine-specific restart ceiling.

question: Attempting to restart the engine with a stationary propeller, above approximately what airspeed will the propeller of a TAE 125-01 engine begin to rotate by windmilling?
explanation: For the TAE 125-01 engine, accelerating above approximately 105 KIAS starts the propeller windmilling; for the TAE 125-02-99 engine without the dual-mass flywheel modification, the figure is 110 KIAS.

question: When restarting the engine with a stationary propeller by accelerating to windmilling speed, what altitude loss must be expected?
explanation: Accelerating to restart a stopped propeller costs altitude - at least 1000 ft (300 meters) must be expected.

question: On a TAE 125-02-99 engine with the dual-mass flywheel modification (MÄM 40-701) installed, what does a stopped (non-windmilling) propeller after engine failure indicate?

options.text: A minor ECU fault that can be reset with the ECU TEST button
A low oil quantity that will clear once altitude is lost
A major mechanical engine defect - a restart with a stationary propeller shall not be considered
A normal governor response that requires no action

explanation: With the dual-mass flywheel modification the propeller of a failed engine continues windmilling; if it has stopped, this points to a major mechanical defect, and restart with a stationary propeller is not to be attempted.

question: Following a failure of the propeller governor, what RPM should every effort be made not to exceed while adjusting RPM with the power lever?
explanation: After a governor failure the RPM is adjusted using the power lever, taking care not to exceed 2500 RPM.

question: During a propeller overspeed caused by a defective governor, to what RPM should the power lever be reduced?
explanation: With the propeller held at the fine pitch stop by the defective governor, power is reduced so as not to exceed 2300 RPM; if increased climb power is required, up to 2500 RPM is permitted for a maximum of 10 minutes.

question: During a propeller underspeed, to what RPM can the propeller drop, leaving no climb or go-around performance available?
explanation: A propeller underspeed, with the governor holding the blades at the high pitch stop, can drop RPM to 1400 RPM or below - level flight should still be possible except in rough weather.

question: Using the EMERG. TRANSFER position of the emergency fuel valve, at approximately what rate is fuel transferred from the AUX tank to the MAIN tank?
explanation: The engine-driven pump transfers fuel at approximately 18 to 21 US gal/h (70 to 80 liters/h) when EMERG. TRANSFER is selected - much slower than the normal electric transfer pump's approximately 60 US gal/h.

question: When using the emergency fuel valve's EMERG. TRANSFER position, by what point must it be switched back to NORMAL?

options.text: Before the main tank indication reads zero
Before the auxiliary tank indication reads zero

explanation: The valve must be returned to NORMAL before the AUX tank reads zero; otherwise the engine will stop in flight once the AUX tank is empty.

question: On engine fire when starting on the ground, after switching the emergency fuel valve OFF, the fuel transfer pump OFF, and ENGINE and ELECTRIC MASTER OFF, what is done once the airplane has come to a standstill?

options.text: Open the canopy and evacuate the airplane immediately
Restart the engine using the stationary propeller procedure
Select ECU B and attempt to taxi clear
Wait for the fire services before opening the canopy

explanation: After standstill, the canopy is opened and the airplane is evacuated immediately.

question: For smoke and fire during take-off, when it cannot be aborted, what airspeed is used before climbing to a safe height to reach the landing area?
explanation: The airspeed given for this scenario at 1150 kg is 73 KIAS - the same best glide/emergency-landing figure used throughout Chapter 3 at max mass.

question: For an engine fire in flight, once it seems certain the selected landing area will be reached, what is done with the emergency fuel valve and the power lever?

options.text: Emergency fuel valve NORMAL, power lever IDLE
Emergency fuel valve EMERG. TRANSFER, power lever MAX
Emergency fuel valve OFF, power lever MAX
Emergency fuel valve OFF, power lever IDLE

explanation: The checklist calls for the emergency fuel valve OFF and the power lever set to MAX, before carrying out the emergency landing with engine off.

question: For an electrical fire with smoke in flight, what does switching the EMERGENCY switch ON achieve?

options.text: It cuts all power to the ECU to stop the fire
It automatically opens the front canopy
It transfers fuel from the AUX tank to the MAIN tank
The emergency battery supplies power to the attitude gyro and the flood light

explanation: Switching the ELECTRIC MASTER OFF kills all electric and electronic equipment, including the attitude gyro; the EMERGENCY switch then supplies the emergency battery to the attitude gyro and flood light only.

question: With the propeller windmilling, what is the DA 40 D's glide ratio, and what horizontal distance does that give for every 1000 ft of altitude lost in still air?
explanation: With the propeller windmilling the glide ratio is 8.8, equivalent to 1.45 NM per 1000 ft of altitude lost; with a stationary propeller the glide ratio improves to 10.3 (1.70 NM per 1000 ft), though that configuration may not be attainable while keeping a safe airspeed.

question: For an emergency landing with the engine off, what governs the target touchdown airspeed?

options.text: Touchdown with flaps UP to extend the float
Touchdown with the lowest possible airspeed
Touchdown at exactly vNE minus 10 KIAS
Touchdown at the normal landing approach speed regardless of flap setting

explanation: The emergency landing with engine off checklist calls for touchdown with the lowest possible airspeed, after selecting flaps LDG once the landing field is certain to be reached.

question: Landing with a defective tire on the main landing gear, which side of the runway should be used, and how should the wing be held?

options.text: Land on the centerline with wings level throughout
Land at the edge on the side of the intact tire, holding the wing on the defective side low
Land at the edge on the side of the intact tire, holding the wing on that side low
Land at the edge on the side of the defective tire, holding that wing low

explanation: Landing on the side of the intact tire, with that wing held low, lets the expected swerve toward the defective tire be corrected on the runway.

question: With defective brakes, what type of landing surface is generally recommended to reduce the landing run?

options.text: A long paved runway, for the smoothest stop
A downslope, to help the airplane decelerate
Grass, for its greater rolling resistance

explanation: A landing on grass is recommended with defective brakes, because its greater rolling resistance reduces the landing run.

question: Recovering from an unintentional spin, which four actions must be carried out immediately and simultaneously?

options.text: Power lever IDLE, rudder full against the spin, elevator fully forward, ailerons neutral
Power lever MAX, rudder full against the spin, elevator fully aft, ailerons neutral
Power lever IDLE, rudder neutral, elevator fully forward, ailerons full against the spin
Power lever IDLE, rudder full with the spin, elevator fully forward, ailerons neutral

explanation: Steps 1 to 4 of spin recovery - power IDLE, full rudder against the direction of spin, elevator fully forward, and ailerons neutral - must be done together; flaps UP follows as step 5.

question: During spin recovery, once rotation has stopped and the airplane is returned to normal flight, what speed must not be exceeded?
explanation: Recovering from the descent into normal flight attitude, the never-exceed speed of 178 KIAS must not be exceeded.

question: On encountering unintentional icing, why does the checklist call for increased power?

options.text: To keep the coolant temperature in the green range
To maintain the alternator's charging voltage
To prevent ice build-up on the propeller blades
To warm the cabin more quickly

explanation: Power is increased specifically to prevent ice building up on the propeller blades, alongside pitot heat ON, cabin heat ON and Alternate Air OPEN.

question: What effect does ice build-up have that the icing checklist specifically cautions about?

options.text: It has no effect on stalling speed but reduces vNE
It only affects the propeller, not the wing

explanation: The CAUTION under the icing procedure states plainly that ice build-up increases the stalling speed.

question: If the Pitot heating fails while in icing conditions, what should be done with the Alternate Static valve?

options.text: Open it, and close the emergency windows
Close it, and open the emergency windows
Leave it closed and land immediately
Open it, and open the emergency windows

explanation: A Pitot heating failure in icing conditions means a loss of static instruments is expected; the Alternate Static valve is opened and the emergency windows are closed.

question: In a complete failure of the electrical system, after checking the circuit breakers, what is the next step?

options.text: Switch ELECTRIC MASTER OFF then ON again

explanation: After checking circuit breakers, the ESSENTIAL BUS switch is turned ON; if power is still unavailable, the EMERGENCY switch is used next.

question: How long can the batteries be expected to remain the last source of electrical power after an alternator failure?
explanation: An alternator failure leaves the batteries as the last remaining source of electrical power for a minimum of 30 minutes.

question: If a voltage in the red range (above 15.5 V or below 11 V) is indicated, what is the recommended action?

options.text: Switch essential bus OFF and continue the flight as planned
Reset the ECU by cycling ENGINE MASTER OFF then ON
Select ECU B and continue to the original destination
Switch essential bus ON and land on the nearest appropriate airfield

explanation: A red-range voltage calls for the essential bus to be switched ON and a landing at the nearest appropriate airfield.

question: On suspicion of carbon monoxide contamination in the cabin, to what airspeed should the pilot reduce before unlatching the front canopy?
explanation: 120 KIAS is the maximum demonstrated airspeed for opening the front canopy in flight, so airspeed is reduced below that before unlatching it to the 'Cooling Gap' position.

question: If the DOOR warning light illuminates and the rear door is found unlocked, what airspeed limit applies before landing at the next suitable airfield?
explanation: With the rear door unlocked, airspeed is kept below 140 KIAS and a landing is made at the next suitable airfield; the pilot must not attempt to lock the door in flight, since the safety latch may disengage and the door separate.
